title: Docker: main layout
question: Which layout should the Docker plugin use?

variants.label: Tabs + grouped table
variants.notes: Resource tabs on top (Containers, Stacks, Images, Volumes, Networks, Templates, Registries, Cleanup). Containers in a table grouped by stack, with live CPU sparkline, ports, update badges, quick actions, stack-level Restart and Edit compose, multi-select bar. Shown on real-looking data: 3 compose stacks plus standalone containers, one unhealthy, one in a restart loop, image updates available.

variants.label: Sidebar + stack cards
variants.notes: A second sidebar inside the plugin groups Workloads, Resources and Tools. Containers as cards per stack with CPU, memory, uptime and a live chart. More visual, less dense. Shown on real-looking data: 3 compose stacks plus standalone containers, one unhealthy, one in a restart loop, image updates available.

variants.label: Health first + list
variants.notes: Summary cards on top (containers, total CPU and memory, things that need attention, disk you can free), resource tabs as a segmented bar, then a flat list with a coloured state strip and the stack as a tag. Shown on real-looking data: 3 compose stacks plus standalone containers, one unhealthy, one in a restart loop, image updates available.
